articles.text: HÚ XIĀNSHENG: Nǐ jiāli yǒu shénme rén?
MR. HÚ: What people are there in your family?
WÁNG TÀITAI: Yǒu wǒ xiānsheng gēn sānge háizi.
MRS. WÁNG: There's my husband and three children.
HÚ XIĀNSHENG: Shì nánháizi, shì nǚháizi?
MR. HÚ: Are they boys or girls?
WÁNG TÀITAI: Yǒu liǎngge nánháizi, yíge nǚháizi. Nǐmen yǒu jǐge háizi?
MRS. WÁNG: There are two boys and one girl. How many children do you have?
HÚ XIĀNSHENG: Wǒmen jiù yǒu liǎngge nǚháizi, méiyou nánháizi.
MR. HÚ: We have only two girls, no boys.
WÁNG TÀITAI: Nǐmen háizi dōu zài zhèli ma?
MRS. WÁNG: Are all your children here?
HÚ XIĀNSHENG: Bù, yíge zài zhèli, yíge hái zài Měiguó. Nǐ yǒu xiōngdì jiěmèi ma?
MR. HÚ: No, one is here, and one is still in America. Do you have brothers and sisters?
WÁNG TÀITAI: Wǒ jiù yǒu yíge gēge, méiyou jiějie.
MRS. WÁNG: I have only one older brother, no older sister.
